Title: Some doubts on steal blood and others

Messages.Author: Pedro Miguel Valerio Ramos
Messages.Body:
Hi...
In my gaming group we're having some soubts about some cards and some rules.
Anyone to make things a bit more cleran to us ? ;)

1st: Can damage from combat cards that steal blood be prevented (by
fortitude cards) or dodged in any way ?

2nd: Blood to Water, asks for the opposing vampire to BURN blood before
strikes are delivered. Can the vampire prevent burning that blood with
fortitude cards ?

3rd: Does a Vampire has to take an action to burn " Blood Tears of ???" (a
new AH card that either gives 2 blood to the vampire, or prevents 2 points of
damage) ?

4th: (this one is a really stupid one, but here it goes...) After a
vampire tries to block an action without beeing successful, can other
vampires try to block the action at the point where it was left (with the
stealth the action has) ?

5th: Imagine a vampire atempts that take an action that requires him to pay
blood (like Sensory Deprivation). A vampire atempts to block the action.
The acting vampire plays a +1 stealth card that makes him pay one more
blood, but the blocking vampire plays an intercept card and the action is
blocked. Question is: Does the acting vampire pays 4 points of blood (3
from Sensory Dep., and 1 from the stealth card) or 1 point only (from the
stealth he put in the action) or no blood at all ? We've been using the
2nd choice, but we're not sure if that's the correct one (morons we are...).

I guess that's it for now...

Thanx in advance for your help...

Pedro

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
fahnuir@student (Pedro Miguel Valerio Ramos) writes:

>Hi...
>In my gaming group we're having some soubts about some cards and some rules.
>Anyone to make things a bit more cleran to us ? ;)

>1st: Can damage from combat cards that steal blood be prevented (by
>fortitude cards) or dodged in any way ?

No. There's no such thing as "damage" from a steal blood strike.
Steal blood doesn't cause damage - it moves blood (or life) from
a minion to the vampire. In the same way that Steal Equipment
would not be considered damage.

>2nd: Blood to Water, asks for the opposing vampire to BURN blood before
>strikes are delivered. Can the vampire prevent burning that blood with
>fortitude cards ?

No, again it is not damage. If the vampire has insufficient blood,
the excess "burn" is ignored (whereas, if the burn were damage, the
vampire would be sent to torpor for failing to burn enough blood to
heal all of the damage).

>3rd: Does a Vampire has to take an action to burn " Blood Tears of ???" (a
>new AH card that either gives 2 blood to the vampire, or prevents 2 points of
>damage) ?

No.

>4th: (this one is a really stupid one, but here it goes...) After a
>vampire tries to block an action without beeing successful, can other
>vampires try to block the action at the point where it was left (with the
>stealth the action has) ?

Yes.

>5th: Imagine a vampire atempts that take an action that requires him to pay
>blood (like Sensory Deprivation). A vampire atempts to block the action.
>The acting vampire plays a +1 stealth card that makes him pay one more
>blood, but the blocking vampire plays an intercept card and the action is
>blocked. Question is: Does the acting vampire pays 4 points of blood (3
>from Sensory Dep., and 1 from the stealth card) or 1 point only (from the
>stealth he put in the action) or no blood at all ? We've been using the
>2nd choice, but we're not sure if that's the correct one (morons we are...).

2nd choice is correct. Only the cost for the action is recovered
(actually, it isn't paid at all until the action is successful).

Costs for action modifiers/reaction cards are paid for as the cards are
played, and will not be regained if the action is blocked (or not).
